newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's primary Cetes rates look set to rise.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's primary Cetes rates look set to rise.

text.p: Rates on Mexico's primary Cetes are seen rising at Banco de Mexico's auction on Tuesday, pulled higher by the possibility of rise in U.S. rates during the next meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve, analysts said.
The bellwether 28-day rate is seen rising by up to 75 basis points, after falling last week to 18.37 percent.
Rates on the longer end of the yield-curve could also rise by up to 25 basis points at the auction on Tuesday, analysts said.

"This small rise could come about due to the fact markets are starting to become a little worried before the news that could come out of the United States and the next meeting of the Fed, said Luis Manuel Arcos, an analyst with brokerage house Bursamex.
Market players are also looking at various economic indicators that are expected in the United States this week, which could influence the interest rate trend there.
"Obviously this news could influence the yield on the long-bond and thus on the markets," Arcos added.
The Open Market Committee of the U.S. Federal Reserve is set to meet next on May 20.

Dealers said demand could also fall at the Mexican Cetes auction this week. "Rates are also at very low levels, and are less attractive for investors, so demand could be another factor in this auction," said one analyst.
Last week demand was 13.035 billion pesos worth for the 3.0 billion pesos worth of Cetes on offer.
Banks will also have to square their books with Banco De Mexico this week, which could reduce liquidity in markets and pressure rates, analysts said.
Banco de Mexico will auction 3.0 billion pesos worth of Cetes this week.
